entry.title: Daily Digest — Sunday, June 21, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In ice hockey, the Carolina Hurricanes defeat the Vegas Golden Knights to win the Stanley Cup.
  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.
  • Elon Musk becomes the world's first US-dollar trillionaire after his company SpaceX raises the largest initial public offering.
  • Princess Bajrakitiyabha of Thailand, a possible heir to the throne, dies at the age of 47 after a three-year comatose state.

Did You Know

  • ... that one of the original carvers of a totem pole described efforts to restore it as akin to "sending a carpenter to repaint the Mona Lisa"?
  • ... that Jean Varraud once put football star Zinedine Zidane on cleaning duty?
  • ... that the number of damage claims lodged after the 1974 Dunedin earthquake was unusually high for an earthquake of its magnitude?
  • ... that Richard M. Hotaling maintained a herd of Holstein cattle from Holland at his house in California?
  • ... that the music video for the PinkPantheress song " Girl Like Me " evokes a "pre-Brexit utopia", according to the New Statesman ?
  • ... that a history of New York City examines its subject from the metaphorical viewpoints of a satellite, a jet airliner, a helicopter, a bird, and ground level?
  • ... that Indonesian politician Muhadi Suyono threatened legal action after a Malaysian government website listed reog as one of their cultural traditions?
  • ... that Eiga.com withdrew an April Fool's Day prank mocking Donald Trump?
  • ... that Kris Lindahl 's billboards have been reacted to with anger, annoyance, and fandom?

On This Day

  • 217 BC – Second Punic War : Commanded by Hannibal, the Carthaginians ambushed a Roman army at the Battle of Lake Trasimene, capturing or killing 25,000 men.
  • 1848 – In the Wallachian Revolution, Ion Heliade Rădulescu and Christian Tell proclaimed a new republican government in present-day Romania.
  • 1898 – The United States captured Guam from Spain in a bloodless event during the Spanish–American War.
  • 1948 – The Manchester Baby, the world's first stored-program computer, ran its first program.

Hacker News

  • CSSQuake — A fully playable Quake-like first-person shooter implemented entirely in CSS, with WASD movement, mouse look, dynamic lighting, and particle effects. (discussion, 506 points)
  • The Wholesale Plagiarism of Obscure Sorrows — An unknown party registered a near-identical domain to John Koenig's beloved Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows, republished the entire book's text with AI-generated images replacing Koenig's original artwork, and bolted on an AI word-generator — all without authorization. (discussion, 370 points)

LessWrong

  • Google Can't Math Parsecs by jefftk — Google's calculator gives the correct value for a parsec in meters, but when doing unit math (e.g. 1 AU / 1 arcsecond) it treats the arcsecond as degrees instead of radians, producing a result off by a factor of 57.3 (180/π). (58 karma)

entry.title: Daily Digest — Saturday, June 20, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In ice hockey, the Carolina Hurricanes defeat the Vegas Golden Knights to win the Stanley Cup.
  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.
  • Elon Musk becomes the world's first US-dollar trillionaire after his company SpaceX raises the largest initial public offering.
  • Princess Bajrakitiyabha of Thailand, a possible heir to the throne, dies at the age of 47 after a three-year comatose state.
  • English artist David Hockney dies at the age of 88.

Did You Know

  • ... that comedian Pudgy was often referred to as the "female Don Rickles "?
  • ... that Mexico's Observatorio 1873 began as a military lookout and observatory, and now includes a whale museum, an iguana sanctuary and a zip line?
  • ... that a Hindu wife of the Muslim ruler of Awadh is often linked to a festival honoring Lord Hanuman on Tuesdays ?
  • ... that the Supreme Court of Canada set aside an election in a federal electoral district in Quebec after one postal vote was not counted?
  • ... that Shirakami Fubuki introduced Hololive to global audiences with a drumming showdown?
  • ... that the Neoclassical and Art Deco sections of the Orleans Parish Criminal Courts Building were designed by its architect to represent the elegance and the severity of the law?
  • ... that, in his book The Anatomy of Evil, forensic psychiatrist Michael Stone writes that he suffered from a nightmare after interviewing serial killer Tommy Lynn Sells in Texas?
  • ... that Lai Ka-ying is the first Hongkonger in space, but not the first astronaut born in Hong Kong ?
  • ... that to win a fighting video game, a player must bark loudly and frequently?

On This Day

  • 1837 – Queen Victoria acceded to the British throne, beginning a 63-year reign.
  • 1921 – British Army officer Thomas Stanton Lambert was assassinated by the Irish Republican Army near Moydrum, Ireland.
  • 1959 – The extratropical remnants of an Atlantic hurricane reached the Gulf of St. Lawrence in Canada, causing 22 fishing boats to capsize and killing 35 people.
  • 1979 – Bill Stewart, an American journalist, was executed by Nicaraguan Guardia forces.
  • 1982 – The International Conference on the Holocaust and Genocide, the first major conference in genocide studies, opened despite Turkish attempts to cancel it due to the inclusion of presentations on the Armenian genocide.

Hacker News

  • Hyundai buys Boston Dynamics — Hyundai acquires SoftBank's remaining 9.65% stake in Boston Dynamics for $325M, giving it full ownership of the humanoid robotics firm as it prepares to deploy the electric Atlas robot in its Georgia EV factory by 2028. (discussion, 833 points)
  • Norway imposes near ban on AI in elementary school — Norway has moved to sharply restrict AI use in elementary schools, signaling a growing regulatory appetite among governments to limit AI's role in early education. (discussion, 675 points)
  • Google workspace threatening to block Firefox access — Google Workspace began displaying warnings to Firefox users urging them to switch to Chrome, with support claiming it affects only the admin console and is a "recommendation" — but offering no public documentation. (discussion, 484 points)
  • There are no instances in ATProto — A clear explainer on why ATProto (the protocol underlying Bluesky) fundamentally differs from Mastodon's federated-instance model: in ATProto, hosting and aggregation are decoupled, so your identity isn't tied to any single server. (discussion, 452 points)
  • AI Engineer Claims to Have Cracked Linear A — Self-taught AI engineer Tom Di Mino claims to have deciphered the undecoded Bronze Age Minoan script Linear A, identifying it as an extinct Semitic language ancestral to biblical Hebrew; the claim is under review by linguists at Rutgers and Cambridge. (discussion, 426 points)
  • Bobby Prince, composer for Doom, Wolfenstein 3D, and Duke Nukem 3D, has died — Bobby Prince, the pioneering video game composer whose work defined the sound of 1990s id Software and 3D Realms titles, died June 16, 2026, at age 81; the original Doom soundtrack was selected for preservation in the Library of Congress earlier this year. (discussion, 380 points)
  • How many of the 170k English words do you know? — An interactive vocabulary quiz that estimates how many of the roughly 170,000 English words you know. (discussion, 378 points)
  • Court Records Should Be Free — The EFF backs the Open Courts Act of 2026, which would abolish PACER's fees (currently over $150M/year) and replace its aging system with a modern, unified public platform for federal court records. (discussion, 376 points)

LessWrong

  • The LLM shoggoth meme is weirder than you think by HedonicEscalator — A literary and philosophical essay tracing the "shoggoth" metaphor for LLMs back through Lovecraft's At the Mountains of Madness, arguing the parallel between AI systems and Lovecraft's mindlessly mimetic artificial lifeforms is stranger and richer than the meme typically conveys. (58 karma)

entry.title: Daily Digest — Friday, June 19, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In ice hockey, the Carolina Hurricanes defeat the Vegas Golden Knights to win the Stanley Cup.
  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.
  • Elon Musk becomes the world's first US-dollar trillionaire after his company SpaceX raises the largest initial public offering.
  • Princess Bajrakitiyabha of Thailand, a possible heir to the throne, dies at the age of 47 after a three-year comatose state.
  • English artist David Hockney dies at the age of 88.

Did You Know

  • ... that it was 41 years between the first Ditrichites moss description and the genus being reported in amber fossils ?
  • ... that basketball player Adan Diggs hired an agent before making his high school debut?
  • ... that Johns Hopkins University and the City of Baltimore agreed to demolish the city's former U.S. Marine Hospital in 1987, and then changed their minds in 2019?
  • ... that in the Battle of Faventia, the Byzantines missed the opportunity to attack the Gothic army while crossing a river due to disagreements among their commanders?
  • ... that two relatively unknown players, Cary Brabham and Gordon Laro, were featured on the cover of Madden NFL '96 ?
  • ... that a Tijuana water park features a slide that curves upward to launch riders airborne into a pool?
  • ... that the Mutapa Empire fragmented following the death of a ruler who spent his time writing songs on an mbira and smoking dagga ?
  • ... that Israel D. Andrews believed that promoting trade with the provinces of British North America would eventually lead to U.S. annexation?
  • ... that Olympic cyclist Clyde Rimple was fined £60 for pouring bleach and urinating on his wife's clothes?

On This Day

  • 1718 – An earthquake on the Tibetan Plateau led to the deaths of more than 73,000 people.
  • 1846 – The first officially recorded baseball game in U.S. history using modern rules was played in Hoboken, New Jersey, with the "New York Nine" defeating the New York Knickerbockers 23–1.
  • 1926 – King Roger, an opera about Roger II of Sicily by Karol Szymanowski, was premiered at the Grand Theatre in Warsaw.
  • 1965 – Nguyễn Cao Kỳ, the commander of the South Vietnam Air Force, was appointed prime minister at the head of a military regime.
  • 2010 – The royal wedding of Victoria, Crown Princess of Sweden, and Daniel Westling took place in Stockholm Cathedral.

Hacker News

  • I found 10k GitHub repositories distributing Trojan malware — A researcher discovered a large-scale GitHub campaign where thousands of accounts clone legitimate repos and periodically push a new commit adding a link to a malware-laden zip archive that evades VirusTotal's URL scanner but is detected when the zip itself is submitted. (discussion, 802 points)
  • Swiss parliament lifts ban on new nuclear power plants — Switzerland's National Council voted 100–98 to approve a counterproposal to the Blackout Initiative, clearing the way for new nuclear construction after a marathon debate; the measure now goes to a public referendum. (discussion, 757 points)
  • Microsoft new Outlook takes 10 seconds to do what Outlook Classic does instantly — Because the new Outlook is built on WebView2 (a Chromium wrapper around Outlook.com), clicking a Windows 11 email notification takes roughly 10 seconds to navigate to the message, while Outlook Classic does it near-instantly — a performance gap Microsoft has not been able to close with app updates alone. (discussion, 667 points)
  • Emacs 31 is around the corner: The changes I'm daily driving — A developer who has been running Emacs 31 pre-release for months highlights the most useful new built-ins, especially automatic tree-sitter grammar installation (treesit-auto-install-grammar) and a new markdown-ts-mode shipping in core, reducing reliance on external packages. (discussion, 441 points)
  • I told them forced consent was unlawful. 5 years later it cost Elkjop €1.8M — A privacy researcher who complained in 2021 that Elkjop's customer club made unsubscribing from marketing emails impossible without cancelling membership — invalidating GDPR consent requirements — saw Norway's Datatilsynet finally impose a NOK 20 million (~€1.8M) fine in June 2026 for exactly that violation. (discussion, 394 points)
  • CS 6120: Advanced Compilers: The Self-Guided Online Course (2020) — Cornell's graduate compilers course, covering topics like SSA, dataflow analysis, and LLVM, available free as a self-guided online course with video lectures. (discussion, 374 points)
  • The founder of Craigslist has given away half a billion dollars — Craig Newmark, who deliberately kept Craigslist from becoming a VC-fueled ad machine, has now donated $500M to charity since the site launched and signed the Giving Pledge, pushing back publicly against billionaires like Peter Thiel who have been discouraging philanthropic commitments. (discussion, 365 points)
  • Show HN: Are You in the Weights? — A tool that appears to let users check whether their data or content is represented in AI model weights. (discussion, 350 points)

LessWrong

  • Your Model Organisms Might Be Fried by Daniel Tan — The Arcadia Alignment "model motivations" team argues that existing alignment model organisms (fine-tuned to exhibit pathologies like secret loyalties or reward hacking) are behaviorally degraded in unrelated ways — losing preference coherence and instruction-following — making them poor proxies for real deployment models and confounding the interpretability and auditing work built on them. (70 karma)
  • GDM AI Control Roadmap by Mary Phuong — Google DeepMind has published a v0.1 AI Control Roadmap outlining a tiered system of detection and prevention invariants — drawing on the MITRE ATT&CK framework via a new taxonomy called TRAIT&R — to guard against adversarial AI behavior in internal deployments as models grow more capable. (60 karma)

entry.title: Daily Digest — Thursday, June 18, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In ice hockey, the Carolina Hurricanes defeat the Vegas Golden Knights to win the Stanley Cup.
  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.
  • Elon Musk becomes the world's first US-dollar trillionaire after his company SpaceX raises the largest initial public offering.
  • Princess Bajrakitiyabha of Thailand, a possible heir to the throne, dies at the age of 47 after a three-year comatose state.
  • English artist David Hockney dies at the age of 88.

Did You Know

  • ... that the Wangdue Phodrang Dzong was destroyed by a fire in 1837, damaged by an earthquake in 1897 and destroyed again by a fire in 2012?
  • ... that Bahu Begum gave up her nose ring with pearls for her husband's sovereignty?
  • ... that facial dysmorphism and moderate intellectual disability are symptoms of 49,XXYYY syndrome ?
  • ... that Walt Whitman Park was the site of the first playground built on public parkland for children of U.S. government workers?
  • ... that the original Trickcal: Chibi Go shut down only two hours after it was released?
  • ... that in 2018, Alec Radford was the lead author on OpenAI's research paper on generative pre-trained transformers, which form the foundation of ChatGPT?
  • ... that the Jay Chou album Children of the Sun was named after a note he got with a box of mangoes?
  • ... that Jan Djong was fired from his post one day after his supporters held a demonstration in his support?
  • ... that Take-Two Interactive filed a trademark claim against It Takes Two ?

On This Day

  • 618 – Sui–Tang transition : Chinese governor Li Yuan declared himself emperor, establishing the Tang dynasty.
  • 1858 – Charles Darwin received a manuscript by fellow naturalist Alfred Russel Wallace on natural selection, which encouraged him to publish his own theory of evolution.
  • 1940 – World War II : Charles de Gaulle gave his Appeal of 18 June speech, often considered to be the origin of the French Resistance.
  • 1953 – A Douglas C-124 Globemaster II aircraft crashed just after takeoff from Tachikawa, Japan, killing all 129 people on board.
  • 2012 – Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud was appointed the crown prince of Saudi Arabia.

Hacker News

  • Lore – Open source version control system designed for scalability — Epic Games open-sourced Lore, a next-generation VCS built for large-scale projects, featuring chunked storage for big files, on-demand sparse workspaces, and lightweight branching. (discussion, 1150 points)
  • Sixty percent of US consumers say 'AI' in brand messaging is a turnoff — A survey finds that a majority of consumers find AI-branded products off-putting and feel the internet has become less human over the past decade. (discussion, 1042 points)
  • Midjourney Medical — Midjourney is building a whole-body ultrasound scanner — a ring of 500,000 tiny transducers that users descend through in a pool of water in under 60 seconds — aiming to make detailed 3D body imaging as casual and accessible as an MRI but far cheaper. (discussion, 770 points)
  • Volkswagen started blocking GrapheneOS users — VW's app now refuses to work on GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused Android fork, raising concerns about automakers gatekeeping vehicle access based on OS choice. (discussion, 690 points)
  • Want your images back? That'll be $5 — A writer paid Photobucket's $5/month subscription to retrieve childhood photos from the old image host, only to discover his account was empty — a cautionary tale about paywalled user data and predatory subscription dark patterns. (discussion, 634 points)
  • AI demands more engineering discipline. Not less — Charity Majors argues that AI-generated code reaching "median engineer" quality since late 2025 raises the bar for engineering practices rather than lowering it, drawing parallels to the shift from hand-managed servers to immutable infrastructure. (discussion, 383 points)
  • Only 16 Percent of Americans Think AI Will Have a Positive Impact on Society — A Pew Research study finds that despite growing daily AI use (ChatGPT now at 44% of US adults), only 16% of Americans expect a positive societal impact, with young people and women most skeptical and two-thirds believing development is moving too fast. (discussion, 380 points)
  • RFC 10008: The new HTTP Query Method — The IETF has finalized RFC 10008, adding a QUERY HTTP method that allows safe, idempotent requests with a body — filling the long-standing gap between GET (no body) and POST (not idempotent) for complex search and query operations. (discussion, 375 points)
  • Leaked financial docs show OpenAI is losing billions of dollars a year — Audited financials show OpenAI's revenue grew from $3.7B (2024) to $13B (2025), but R&D costs alone hit $19B and total operating losses reached $20.9B, with the company still targeting profitability by 2030. (discussion, 353 points)

LessWrong

  • Gears for political races by Tom Smith — After volunteering on a congressional campaign, the author lays out a ground-level mechanistic case for why US electoral politics is high-impact for AI safety, anchored by data points like ~2% of open-seat primaries being decided by under 100 votes and canvassing yielding roughly 1/3 of a vote per hour. (96 karma)
  • The Once And Future Fable #3: Fix This Code by Zvi — Zvi reports that the government action against Anthropic's Fable 5 model was triggered by the prompt "fix this code" applied to deliberately planted vulnerabilities, with the only outside expert to review the report concluding it should never have triggered export controls. (58 karma)
  • Several frontier models are substantially prefill aware by yeedrag — A new paper finds that multiple frontier LLMs can detect when their assistant-turn content has been tampered with (prefill awareness), even in low-stakes scenarios, raising concerns that this capability could confound safety evaluations and pre-deployment testing. (54 karma)

entry.title: Daily Digest — Wednesday, June 17, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In ice hockey, the Carolina Hurricanes defeat the Vegas Golden Knights to win the Stanley Cup.
  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.
  • Elon Musk becomes the world's first US-dollar trillionaire after his company SpaceX raises the largest initial public offering.
  • Princess Bajrakitiyabha of Thailand, a possible heir to the throne, dies at the age of 47 after a three-year comatose state.

Did You Know

  • ... that SN 2025pht was one of the brightest supernovae observed in 2025?
  • ... that Muwaffaq al-Din Yaqub ibn Siqlab was fluent in Classical Greek and regularly recited passages from Galen to inform his medical treatments?
  • ... that a song uses satire in Spanish and English to critique anti-Mexican sentiment in the U.S. and anti-American sentiment in Mexico?
  • ... that Dutch colonial presence in Mandailing territory began at Kotanopan, Northern Sumatra?
  • ... that lawyer Guillaume Alexandre Tronson du Coudray was assigned to defend Marie Antoinette just two days before her trial began?
  • ... that Mavety Media Group, an adult-oriented publishing company, once published a teen magazine?
  • ... that, four years after Julien Nuijten won the largest award ever earned at a Magic: The Gathering tournament, he won four times as much playing poker?
  • ... that the Amherstburg First Baptist Church was founded by escaped slaves?
  • ... that college football player Grayson McCall attended a media-day session wearing a shirt that said "I piss teal"?

On This Day

  • 653 – Pope Martin I was arrested in the Lateran Palace, Rome, and taken to Constantinople.
  • 1579 – Explorer Francis Drake landed in a region of present-day California, naming it New Albion and claiming it for England.
  • 1919 – Hundreds of Canadian soldiers rioted in Epsom, England, leading to the death of a British police officer.
  • 1972 – Five men were arrested for attempted burglary on the offices of the Democratic National Committee, igniting the Watergate scandal that ultimately led to the resignation of US president Richard Nixon more than two years later.

Hacker News

  • GrapheneOS has been ported to Android 17 — The privacy-focused Android fork has completed its port to Android 17 with official releases coming soon. (discussion, 946 points)
  • Sixty percent of US consumers say 'AI' in brand messaging is a turnoff — A new survey finds that consumers increasingly feel the internet has become less human, and that AI branding actively repels rather than attracts them. (discussion, 668 points)
  • Is Meta destroying its engineering organization? — The Pragmatic Engineer reports that Meta's leadership has dismantled its decades-long high-performance engineering culture in just weeks, driven by an AI-fueled push that has turned engineering from a profit center into a disdained cost center. (discussion, 621 points)
  • GLM-5.2 is the new leading open weights model on Artificial Analysis — Z.ai's 744B-parameter GLM-5.2 scores 51 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1, surpassing MiniMax-M3 and DeepSeek V4 Pro, and matches proprietary models like GPT-5.5 on agentic benchmarks while remaining cost-competitive. (discussion, 546 points)
  • TIL: You can make HTTP requests without curl using Bash /dev/TCP — Bash's built-in /dev/tcp pseudo-device lets you open raw TCP sockets and hand-craft HTTP requests entirely in shell, useful for debugging in stripped-down container images where curl isn't available. (discussion, 511 points)
  • Apple is about to make Hide My Email useless — Apple is moving Hide My Email and Sign in with Apple aliases to the @private.icloud.com subdomain, making it trivial for services to block all relay addresses in bulk, undermining the privacy feature's core value. (discussion, 505 points)
  • Stop Using JWTs — A well-circulated argument that JWTs are misused as session tokens when they were designed for short-lived single-use cases, and that standard cookie-based sessions are more secure and appropriate for keeping users logged in. (discussion, 461 points)
  • Want your images back? Sure... That'll be $5! — A writer recounts trying to retrieve childhood photos from Photobucket, only to find them paywalled behind a subscription disguised as a one-time $5 fee — and then discovering his account had no images anyway. (discussion, 444 points)
  • U.S. pulling ocean sensors a 'shock' for Canadian research as El Niño nears — The U.S. is removing ocean monitoring sensors, disrupting Canadian climate and El Niño research that depends on shared observational infrastructure. (discussion, 439 points)
  • Has AI already killed self-help nonfiction books? — Tim Ferriss shares BookScan data showing his catalog's print sales have collapsed ~80% since 2022, with the steepest drops tracking directly to LLM adoption, arguing that AI has functionally replaced the lookup-table and decision-tree value of prescriptive self-help books. (discussion, 382 points)
  • Hacker News but for Independent Blogs — Bubbles.town is a community front page aggregating posts from over 5,000 independent personal blogs, ranked by votes and freshness. (discussion, 364 points)
  • Epic Games announces Lore version control system — Epic Games has open-sourced Lore, a next-generation version control system designed for large files, on-demand sparse workspaces, and centralized caching — targeting game development workflows that strain Git and Perforce. (discussion, 353 points)

LessWrong

  • Guardian Angels: LLM Personalization for Productivity and Security by gwern — Proposes "Guardian Angel" LLMs — personalized digital twins trained to emulate a single user's values and preferences — as a way to solve the principal-agent problem, boost knowledge-worker productivity, and defend against AI-powered spearphishing and propaganda attacks. (72 karma)
  • Scaling Hypothesis #2: Are Humans Just More Over-Parameterized? by gwern — Argues that human brains achieve robust generalization through extreme overparameterization and high-learning-rate training on small, filtered datasets — a bias-minimizing "catapult" strategy opposite to LLMs' variance-minimizing approach — and that replicating this in AI could yield adversarial robustness and better alignment. (61 karma)

entry.title: Daily Digest — Tuesday, June 16, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.

  • Princess Bajrakitiyabha of Thailand, a possible heir to the throne, dies at the age of 47 after a three-year comatose state.
  • English artist David Hockney dies at the age of 88.
  • In athletics, Ja'Kobe Tharp sets a new world record in men's 110 metres hurdles.

Did You Know

  • ... that Talbot Street Baptist Church was painted red, which was the style at the time, only to have its original polychrome brickwork restored later?
  • ... that a case of mistaken identity made actress Camila Ashland the target of a flood of protesting phone calls?
  • ... that the 1935 Kentucky State Thorobreds won a black college football national championship with "Tarzan" playing quarterback?
  • ... that the letters of British colonial administrator William Henry Sleeman were posthumously published in 1858 to exonerate him during the Indian Rebellion ?
  • ... that Olivia Rodrigo secretly premiered her song " Begged " at an invite-only show with a no-phones policy?
  • ... that fencer Rodolfo da Ponte was selected to compete for Paraguay at the 1968 Summer Olympics after the rowing and football teams did not qualify?
  • ... that US president Warren G. Harding died less than two months after selling his newspaper ?
  • ... that Elsie Eiler, the only resident of Monowi, Nebraska, is also the city's mayor, tavernkeeper, and librarian?
  • ... that David Attenborough's 100th birthday was marked by the naming of a new genus of wasps after him and the announcement that he would narrate Blue Planet III ?

On This Day

  • 1755 – After a two-week siege, the French commander of Fort Beauséjour in present-day New Brunswick, Canada, surrendered to British forces, marking the end of Father Le Loutre's War.
  • 1883 – In the Victoria Hall disaster, 183 children were crushed to death when they ran down the stairs to collect gifts after a variety show in Sunderland, England.
  • 1960 – Psycho, a psychological horror film directed by Alfred Hitchcock and based on a novel of the same name by Robert Bloch, premiered.
  • 1963 – Aboard Vostok 6, Soviet cosmonaut Valentina Tereshkova became the first woman in space.
  • 2016 – Jo Cox, a British Member of Parliament, was murdered in her constituency.

Hacker News

  • Iroh 1.0 — The peer-to-peer networking library built on QUIC reaches its 1.0 milestone, offering a stable API for building distributed applications. (discussion, 1199 points)
  • A backdoor in a LinkedIn job offer — A developer recounts receiving a malicious "technical assessment" via LinkedIn that contained backdoored code, a reminder that supply-chain and social-engineering attacks now target hiring pipelines. (discussion, 1194 points)
  • Ask HN: Has anyone replaced Claude/GPT with a local model for daily coding? — A high-engagement thread exploring real-world experiences running local LLMs as day-to-day coding assistants instead of hosted API services. (discussion, 1003 points)
  • TinyWind: A pixel pirate sailing game with real wind physics (380k+ kms sailed) — A browser-based sailing game that simulates real wind patterns and has clocked over 380,000 km of in-game distance across its player base. (discussion, 844 points)
  • Banned Book Library in a Wi-Fi Smart Light Bulb — A hardware hacker embeds a collection of banned books into a smart bulb's firmware, serving them over the bulb's own Wi-Fi hotspot. (discussion, 389 points)

LessWrong

  • A frontier AI company should shut down by MichaelDickens — Argues that at least one leading AI lab ought to voluntarily cease frontier development given current safety uncertainty. (111 karma)
  • The Once And Future Fable #2 by Zvi — Second installment in Zvi's ongoing narrative series exploring AI and rationality themes through allegorical storytelling. (67 karma)
  • Does preservation make sense before we know how to revive? by Aurelia — Examines whether cryonic or biological preservation is rational to pursue when revival technology remains entirely speculative. (51 karma)

entry.title: Daily Digest — Monday, June 15, 2026
entry.content:
Topics in the News

  • In basketball, the New York Knicks defeat the San Antonio Spurs to win the NBA Finals.
  • Elon Musk becomes the world's first US-dollar trillionaire after his company SpaceX raises the largest initial public offering.
  • English artist David Hockney dies at the age of 88.
  • In athletics, Ja'Kobe Tharp sets a new world record in men's 110 metres hurdles.

Did You Know

  • ... that a world-championship-medalist swimmer called his sport "one of the dullest in existence"?
  • ... that the houses in New York City's Henderson Place Historic District have been described as "gingerbread-type" and likened to dollhouse architecture?
  • ... that actor Erwan Kepoa Falé said that sex was his escape from grief after the death of his father?
  • ... that "almost every road in Sikka had campaign posts" during the 2018 regency election campaign?
  • ... that the title of the 2026 album The World Is to Dig was inspired by a 1952 children's book ?
  • ... that John Kinsey remained speaker of the New Jersey colonial assembly despite moving to Pennsylvania?
  • ... that nighttime programming on Romania's Tele7ABC in 2000 consisted of the poet Adrian Păunescu and a "crumpled blue curtain"?
  • ... that, when James Baker was U.S. secretary of state, he banned Benjamin Netanyahu from the department's headquarters?
  • ... that softball player Laura Taylor scored only four home runs in high school, but then became one of the top home run-hitters in college history?

On This Day

  • 1520 – Leo X issued the papal bull Exsurge Domine, censuring 41 propositions from Martin Luther 's Ninety-five Theses and subsequent writings, and threatening him with excommunication unless he recanted.
  • 1896 – A magnitude-8.5 earthquake and a subsequent tsunami struck Japan, killing at least 22,000 people and destroying about 9,000 homes.
  • 1920 – Three African-American circus workers were lynched by a mob in Duluth, Minnesota, a crime that shocked the country for having taken place in the Northern United States.
  • 1991 – An eruption of Mount Pinatubo in the Philippines deposited large amounts of particulate matter into the atmosphere, enough to briefly lower global temperatures by about 0.5 °C (0.9 °F).
  • 2006 – US president George W. Bush designated 140,000 square miles (360,000 km 2 ) around the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands as the Papahānaumokuākea Marine National Monument, now one of the world's largest protected areas.
